_transcription: PAGE MAP: the booklet is 16 rendered pages (idx 0-15 = printed folios 1-16), every one accounted for. idx 0 = bilingual cover (Series AABB5/5, SET No. 1, Q.P. Code 57/5/1, BIOLOGY (Theory), 2 hours, 35 marks, 15 printed pages, 13 questions). ENGLISH = the EVEN indices 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14 (folios 3-15). HINDI = the ODD indices 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13. The tops of all seven odd indices open in Hindi (idx 1 Hindi instructions and Q1-3, idx 3 Hindi Q4, idx 5 Hindi Q6, idx 7 Hindi Section B / Q7, idx 9 Hindi Q10(b), idx 11 Hindi Section C / Q13(a), idx 13 Hindi Q13(b)), so no English overflow onto an odd page and no parity inversion. idx 14 is English (Q13(b) in full); idx 15 (folio 16) is blank apart from a rule and the footer, checked at full size. The paper is born-digital and its text layer was diffed against the vision read: the two agree on every English line, but the text layer carries none of the figure labels (the S.T.P. boxes, the graph axes, the pie chart, the pBR322 map, the bar graph), so all of those were read off the page. Decimals: the paper prints ORDINARY full stops ('2.5 mg/kg', byte 0x2E in the text layer), so they are left as printed; the scheme prints '1·15' with a raised dot, which is the scheme's own typography. Structure as printed: Section A Q1-6 @2, Section B Q7-12 @3, Section C Q13 case-based @5 = 35. Instruction (iv) says internal choices exist but gives no count; the roster was built from the scheme's bare ORs and each confirmed against a printed OR on the paper: Q3, Q6, Q10 and Q13 (four alternatives). The '//' inside the scheme's Q9 answer is an alternative FORM of the answer (a PCR diagram), not an internal choice. Q13(a) is a case study with three sub-parts, one row each, carrying the scheme's split 1/2/2. Its OR, Q13(b), replaces the WHOLE case study with a DIFFERENT case study (an RNAi passage with its own bar graph and sub-parts (i)-(iii), scheme split 1/1/3), so it is ONE row Q13b, alternative to Q13ai, with its own passage in context and its own setId (CS2), the shape of 2022 57/2/1 Q13b. That RNAi passage is a RE-AUTHORED version of 57/2/1's (different wording, sub-parts and graph legend), so it was transcribed fresh and will not dedup. Q4's two boxed flow diagrams (municipal sewage through two treatment boxes to a river) are carried as text lines joined by arrows per SCIENCE_ADDENDUM 7; the drawn building and river carry no data. Quotes straight as printed; scientific names plain (Parthenium and Cynomolgus print bold, Meloidogyne incognitia bold italic). Typos kept as printed: Q3(a) 'cocain', Q10(b)(ii) 'Extinction of species across taxa are not random.', Q13(a) passage 'Cloning of genes, play' and 'one such engineered vectors', Q13(b) passage 'An experiment was carried to study', Q13(b)(i) 'brings an effect', Q13(b)(iii) 'incognitia' (NCERT: Meloidogyne incognita). Two questions ask the student to draw (Q10(a)(i) the species-area graph, Q13(a)(iii) the EcoRI fragments), so two _drawFigure. No question examines content the rationalised NCERT book removed, so no _outOfSyllabus.

questions.stem: Ringworm is one of the most common infectious fungal disease in humans. Name any two genera of fungi which cause ringworm and state any of its two symptoms.
Can we use slurry of human excreta instead of cowdung slurry to produce biogas in a typical biogas plant? Support your answer giving reasons.
questions._flag: The scheme expects 'No' and accepts 'in human excreta Methanogens or Methanobacteria are absent' as the reason. That reason is too strong: methanogens (e.g. Methanobrevibacter smithii) do live in the human gut, and biogas plants fed with human excreta exist. The board's answer rests on the NCERT point that cattle dung is rich in methanogens. The solution gives the expected answer and brackets the over-strong reason.

Enumerate four most common warning signs of drug and alcohol abuse amongst the youth.

Study the given diagram of Sewage Treatment Plant (S.T.P.) and answer the questions that follow :
S.T.P. (Sewage Treatment Plant) (A): Municipal Sewage \(\rightarrow\) (W) BIOLOGICAL TREATMENT \(\rightarrow\) (X) SEDIMENTATION AND FILTRATION \(\rightarrow\) River
S.T.P. (Sewage Treatment Plant) (B): Municipal Sewage \(\rightarrow\) (Y) SEQUENTIAL FILTRATION \(\rightarrow\) (Z) BIOLOGICAL TREATMENT \(\rightarrow\) River
(a) Which one of the two 'S.T.P.' (A) or (B) will be more effective in treating the human excreta in the municipal waste?
(b) Write the steps followed in carrying the treatment of the sewage in step (Z), once the BOD of sewage is reduced significantly till it is passed on to the "anaerobic sludge digesters".

(i) Which of the two graphs depicts tropical region and temperate regions respectively ?
(ii) Which of the two regions (X) or (Y) will show high biological diversity and why?
questions._figure: REQUIRED: four small graphs side by side, each of Solar radiation (y, arrow upward) against Time of the day (x, ticks 1 hr., 12, 24 hr.), each with one hump-shaped curve peaking at 12; the first two are captioned June 22 and Dec. 22 under the label (X), the last two June 22 and Dec. 22 under the label (Y). How tall each hump is, and so how much each region's radiation changes between June and December, is what part (i) asks the student to read, so it is withheld here. Page idx 6.

questions.subtopic: Species Numbers and Patterns of Biodiversity
questions.stem:
Given below is an equation describing the Species-Area relationship between species richness and area for a wide variety of taxa as angiosperm plants, birds, bats etc.
\(S = CA^{Z}\)
(i) Give a graphical representation of the given equation showing Species-Area relationship.
(ii) What does 'S' represent in the given equation ?
(iii) What is the value of 'Z' (regression coefficient) for frugivorous birds and mammals in the tropical forests of different continents ?
questions._drawFigure: the species-area graph: species richness (S) on the y-axis against area (A) on the x-axis, a curve rising steeply and then levelling off (a rectangular hyperbola) labelled S = CA^Z; the log-log form, a straight line labelled log S = log C + Z log A, may also be shown.

questions.context:
RNA interference (RNAi) holds great potential as a therapeutic agent for the treatment of human diseases and as biocontrol agents in controlling pests in the field of agriculture. An experiment was carried to study the use of 'RNAi' for the potential treatment of disorders of cholesterol metabolism. Some people possess genetic mutations with elevated levels of ApoB gene which predisposes them to coronary artery diseases.

Lowering the amount of ApoB can reduce the number of lipoproteins and lower the blood cholesterol.

Tracy Zimmerman and her colleagues used RNAi in 2006 to reduce the level of ApoB in non human primates Cynomolgus monkeys.

One group of monkeys were given RNAi treatment (small interfering RNAs, SiRNAs) (doses 1 mg/kg SiRNAs), second group of monkeys were given RNAi treatment (doses 2.5 mg/kg SiRNAs) and third group of monkeys were injected with saline.

The results of the study are depicted in the graph below :
questions.stem:
(i) How does the treatment with 2.5 mg/kg brings an effect on cholesterol metabolism when compared from 24 hours and 144 hours.
(ii) Write any two natural sources from where dsRNA molecule could be obtained for silencing the specific mRNA.
(iii) How is RNAi used in controlling the infection on the roots of tobacco plants by the nematode Meloidogyne incognitia.
questions._figure: REQUIRED: a bar graph of Relative serum cholesterol (% predose) (y, 0 to 120 in steps of 20) against Time (hours) at 24, 48, 144 and 264 (x), with three bars at each time keyed Saline - X (diagonal hatching), 1 mg/kg - Y (dotted outline) and 2.5 mg/kg - Z (solid grey). The bar heights, and so how the 2.5 mg/kg bar changes between 24 and 144 hours, are what part (i) asks the student to read, so they are withheld here. Page idx 14.
